Resolves #21094

Replaces the fixed 10 ms `setTimeout` before reading `tabs.getTabBar().sortZone` in `test/playwright/unit/tab/HeaderActions.spec.mjs` with `await expect.poll(() => bar.sortZone).toBeTruthy()`, matching `test/playwright/unit/draggable/container/SortZone.spec.mjs:45` so slow or cold dynamic imports in `Neo.container.Base#afterSetDragResortable` (`loadSortZoneModule()`) cannot race `sortZone` instantiation.

Evidence: L1 (Playwright unit suite on Node/V8 runtime, including single-worker 3x repeat run) → L1 required (deterministic unit test readiness synchronization).

Micro-review eligible: mechanical — single unit-spec readiness poll replacing a fixed 10 ms sleep.

# PR Micro-Review

**Class:** mechanical. A single unit-spec readiness wait replaces a fixed sleep, with no production code touched and no concept to teach.

**Verdict:** Approved

**Glance:** The claim is that a 10 ms sleep raced the tab bar's asynchronously created `sortZone`. At head `5a9f6497a2`:
- **The fix:** the diff replaces `HeaderActions.spec.mjs:405-408` (`setTimeout(…, 10)`, then a read of `bar.sortZone`) with `await expect.poll(() => bar.sortZone).toBeTruthy()`.
- **The precedent:** the same poll, character for character, sits at `test/playwright/unit/draggable/container/SortZone.spec.mjs:45`, for the same `dragResortable` owner shape. The spec under fix creates its `TabContainer` with `dragResortable: true`.
- **Why it is safe:** the wait is monotone. It waits for the very condition the old code assumed after 10 ms, so it can only remove a timing failure. If the zone never appears, it still fails, now at the poll with a clearer message.
- **What I looked for:** any other site the repair touches. There is none; the diff is this one block.
- **CI:** every required context is green on this head: unit, components, e2e-engine, build-all and the baselines.
